H3 cells as hex strings

Source: R/read.R
store_h3_hex.Rd

Cells are stored as 64-bit integers (bit64::integer64), the compact form that Parquet filters and sorts fast, and a read returns them as rcs_h3 (integer64 printed as hex). store_h3_hex() converts them to the 15-character hex strings that other H3 tools use.

Usage

store_h3_hex(x, columns = NULL)

Arguments

x

A data frame returned by a read (a tibble or an sf object), or a vector of cells (rcs_h3, bit64::integer64, hex strings or h3o H3).

columns

For a data frame, the columns to convert (tidyselect); NULL converts the cell columns the package adds that are present: h3, h3_main and h3_p<r>.

Value

For a data frame, x with those columns as character; for a vector, a character vector of the same length. NA stays NA. A plain number aborts: it cannot hold an H3 cell.

Examples

cells <- bit64::as.integer64("599686042433355775")
store_h3_hex(cells)
#> [1] "85283473fffffff"

x <- data.frame(id = 1, h3 = cells)
store_h3_hex(x)
#>   id              h3
#> 1  1 85283473fffffff
